assumptions: Gaussian family,common covariance,independent acquisition and fixed exogenous means are supplied model premises,not certified by a finite normality test. Extra historical records,known means/densities,replayable seeds or current factual-input requirements change the interface. Exact known conditional Gaussian probabilities are legitimately used;unknown density estimates are not treated as exact. Affine Gaussian transport has the same information and correct iid law but changes every input;it can win with cheap exact response updates. Known-density maximal coupling/importance mixing,importance weighting for weaker expectation outputs,shared seeds andbest incremental solvers remain legitimate comparators when their access/output contracts hold. No first-recycling-method or priority claim. Finite-grid law is approximate;continuous minimax theorem does not prove finite-grid optimality. Repeated grid migrations accumulate approximation error. No expected bit-complexity or fixed-latency theorem;resolution must already exist in historical records. Gaussian-model/covariance/clipping error needs extra allowances.
